chunks: Sahl, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadhani, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (عليه السلام): 'Ali ibn Mahziyar read to me the letter of your father (عليه السلام) concerning what he obligated upon the owners of estates: half of the sixth after the expenses, and that there is not upon one whose estate does not meet its expenses half of the sixth nor anything other than that.

Then those with us differed regarding that, and they said: 'Khums is obligatory upon the estates after the expenses—meaning the expenses of the estate and its land-tax—not the expenses of the man and his dependants.'
So he (عليه السلام) wrote: 'After his expenses and the expenses of his dependants, and after the land-tax of the ruling authority.'

key_terms.الضِّيَاعِ: estates or landed properties that generate produce or income
key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: khums, the one-fifth due on certain categories of wealth
key_terms.الْمَئُونَةِ: expenses or maintenance costs to be deducted before assessing liability
key_terms.خَرَاجِ السُّلْطَانِ: the land-tax or levy taken by the ruling authority
key_terms.عِيَالِهِ: his dependants whose maintenance is included in deductible expenses
key_terms.نِصْفُ السُّدُسِ: half of one-sixth, a specified fractional due mentioned in the correspondence

ai.seo_question: Are personal and family expenses deducted before khums is calculated on estate income?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of khums on agricultural estates and clarifies what expenses are deducted before its obligation is calculated. The Imam (عليه السلام) explains that the owner's personal expenses, the expenses of his dependants, and the ruler's tax are all considered before determining the due amount.

en.hubeali: Sahl, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Al Hamdany who said,

‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Ali Bin Mahziyar read out a letter of your<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> to me regarding what is Obligated upon the owner of the estate as being half of the sixth, and that there isn’t upon the one who oversees his estate with his expenses, neither half of the sixth nor other than that.

So the ones before us differed in regards to that and they said, ‘The Khums is Obligated upon the estate after the expenditure, the expenses of the estate and its yield, not the expenses of the man and his dependants’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote to him, ‘After its expenditure and his expenditure and of his dependants, and after the taxation of the ruling authorities’.
en.sarwar: 23. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn ‘Abd Rabbihi who has said the following.
“Al-Rida (a.s.) sent a gift to my father and my father wrote to him, “Is there al-Khums on the gift you just sent to me?”
He wrote back to him in answer, “There is no al-Khums on the gift that the recipient of al-Khums has sent to you.”
